title_en: Guotai Junan Securities Co., Ltd., Haikou Binhai Avenue (Tianfu Hotel) Securities Business Department — application for state compensation
ruling_gist_en: In the execution proceedings, after reviewing and finding that the original execution act was based on the parties' execution settlement agreement which had a major defect due to infringement of an outsider's lawful rights and interests, and upon finding that the execution objection raised by the outsider was established, the people's court revoked the original execution act by means of a ruling, restoring the disputed real property, which was not a specific object designated for delivery under a legal instrument, to its pre-execution status. Such ruling and the act thereof do not constitute the illegal infringement as stipulated in the State Compensation Law and the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning Judicial Compensation in Civil and Administrative Litigation.
keywords_en: state compensation; first instance; Supreme People's Court; Hainan Province; legal person; state organ; State Compensation Law; Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning Judicial Compensation in Civil and Administrative Litigation; validity of execution settlement agreement; legality of restitution in execution; elements of state compensation; dismissal of claims; securities repurchase dispute; execution settlement; execution objection; restitution of real property in execution; securities; administrative litigation
full_text_en:
Guotai Junan Securities Co., Ltd.
Haikou Binhai Avenue (Tianfu Hotel) Securities Business Department
— Application for State Compensation

【Ruling Summary】

During the enforcement procedure, where a people's court, upon review, finds that the enforcement settlement agreement between the parties on which the original enforcement act was based contains material defects due to infringement of the lawful rights and interests of a third party not involved in the case, and the objection raised by that third party is sustained, the court may, by written order, revoke the original enforcement act and restore the disputed real property, which is not the specific property designated for delivery under the legal instrument, to its status prior to enforcement. Such order and act do not constitute the unlawful infringement prescribed in the State Compensation Law and the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning Judicial Compensation in Civil and Administrative Litigation.

State Compensation Commission of the Supreme People's Court
State Compensation Decision

(2011) Fa Wei Pei Zi No. 3

Compensation Claimant: Guotai Junan Securities Co., Ltd. Haikou Binhai Avenue (Tianfu Hotel) Securities Business Department. Domicile: 13/F, Block B, Longzhu Building, No. 2 Longkun North Road, Haikou City.
Responsible Person: Tong Junyang, General Manager of the Business Department.
Authorized Agents: Yan Jichuan, lawyer of Hainan Dongfang Guoxin Law Firm.
Wu Gang, staff member of Guotai Junan Investment Management Co., Ltd.

Compensation Obligor: Hainan High People's Court. Domicile: No. 123 Longkun South Road, Haikou City.
Legal Representative: Dong Zhiliang, President of the Court.
Authorized Agents: Wang Zhigang, court official.
Hu Chuncheng, court official.

The compensation claimant, Guotai Junan Securities Co., Ltd. Haikou Binhai Avenue (Tianfu Hotel) Securities Business Department (hereinafter referred to as Guotai Haikou Business Department), dissatisfied with the compensation decision (2011) Qiong Fa Pei Zi No. 1 made by the Hainan High People's Court (hereinafter referred to as Hainan High Court) on July 4, 2011, applied to the State Compensation Commission of this Court for a decision on state compensation. The State Compensation Commission of this Court has lawfully tried this case, and the trial is now concluded.

The requests submitted by Guotai Haikou Business Department to the State Compensation Commission of this Court are as follows: 1. To revoke the compensation decision (2011) Qiong Fa Pei Zi No. 1 of Hainan High Court; 2. To confirm the illegality of the civil order (1999) Qiong Gao Fa Zhi Zi No. 9-16 of Hainan High Court and the enforcement act thereunder (Note: On September 16, 2003, Hainan High Court made civil order (1999) Qiong Gao Fa Zhi Zi No. 9-17, changing the order numbers originally issued under (1999) Qiong Gao Fa Zhi Zi No. 13 uniformly to (1999) Qiong Gao Fa Zhi Zi No. 9; therefore, the original orders (1999) Qiong Gao Fa Zhi Zi No. 13-10, 13-11, 13-12, 13-13, and 13-16 involved in this decision are uniformly expressed as (1999) Qiong Gao Fa Zhi Zi No. 9-10, 9-11, 9-12, 9-13, and 9-16, and are referred to as Orders 9-10, 9-11, 9-12, 9-13, and 9-16 respectively); 3. To request the return of the 7,049.94 square meters of real property in Jingrui Building, Haikou, and its fruits that were illegally recovered by enforcement, and compensation for losses. The main reasons are:

1. According to Article 210 of the Civil Procedure Law, the recovery of enforcement (execution回转) may only be carried out after the judgment, order, or mediation statement that has been fully enforced has been lawfully revoked. When Hainan High Court made Order 9-16, the civil judgment (2002) Qiong Min Yi Zhong Zi No. 2 of Hainan High Court and the civil judgment (2001) Hai Zhong Fa Min Chu Zi No. 77 of Haikou Intermediate People's Court (hereinafter referred to as Haikou Intermediate Court) were still legally effective. Therefore, Hainan High Court, without lawfully retrying the original effective judgments and its own Orders 9-11, 9-12, and 9-13, made Order 9-16 and carried out enforcement recovery based thereon, which violated the law and should be confirmed as unlawful.

2. According to Article 4 of the Interim Provisions on Several Issues Concerning Enforcement Work of Hainan High People's Court, which states: "Where the subject matter of enforcement has been fully disposed of, and a third party raises an objection to the subject matter thereafter, the enforcement court shall no longer review it, but shall inform the third party that they may handle the matter through litigation proceedings as a new dispute." Hainan High Court, in Order 9-16, found the objection of the third party justified, and, despite the enforcement subject matter having been fully disposed of, revoked Orders 9-11, 9-12, and 9-13 and carried out enforcement recovery of the real property that had already been transferred to Guotai Haikou Business Department's name, which violated this provision.

3. After Guotai Haikou Business Department applied to Hainan High Court to enforce the effective civil judgment (1998) Qiong Jing Chu Zi No. 8, and after Guotai Haikou Business Department, in accordance with Order 9-11 of Hainan High Court, completed the registration of the property rights of the debt-offsetting real property under its own name and paid the relevant taxes and fees, Guotai Haikou Business Department lawfully acquired ownership of the debt-offsetting real property, and its property rights should be protected by law. The ordinary creditor's rights of the third parties, the Liquidation Group of the Closed Hainan Development Bank (hereinafter referred to as Haifengxing Liquidation Group) and Hainan Chuangren Real Estate Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Chuangren Company), cannot prevail over such property rights.

4. According to Article 38 of the State Compensation Law, Order 9-16 of Hainan High Court unlawfully revoked the correct, lawful, and effective Orders 9-11, 9-12, and 9-13, causing Guotai Haikou Business Department to lose the lawfully acquired real property, for which state compensation should be provided.

5. According to Article 13 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on the Procedure for the State Compensation Commission to Hear State Compensation Cases, request that Hainan High Court be instructed to present evidence on the legality of its Order 9-16.

Hainan High Court, in its defense to the State Compensation Commission of this Court, argued: 1. The reasons asserted by Guotai Haikou Business Department that Order 9-16 was unlawful and that compensation should be granted are untenable; 2. Order 9-16 was not actually based on the civil judgment (2003) Hai Zhong Fa Min Zai Zi No. 37 of Haikou Intermediate Court; 3. Guotai Haikou Business Department's creditor's rights have been transferred, and Guotai Junan Investment Management Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Guotai Investment Company) has already declared these claims in the bankruptcy liquidation of Hainan International Leasing Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Haiguozu Company), so Guotai Haikou Business Department should not apply for state compensation. The main reasons are:

1. The reasons asserted by Guotai Haikou Business Department that Order 9-16 was unlawful and that compensation should be granted are untenable. (1) Order 9-16 merely corrected errors in the previous enforcement orders and did not change the original enforcement basis, so no retrial procedure was required. (2) The basis for Guotai Haikou Business Department's application for enforcement was the judgment (1998) Qiong Jing Chu Zi No. 8 of this Court; the securities repurchase funds and interest determined in that judgment are its lawful claims and the subject matter of enforcement. However, the part of the real property in Jingrui Building involved in the original enforcement proceedings (hereinafter referred to as the disputed real property) was not the claim determined in the judgment in favor of Guotai Haikou Business Department. (3) The disputed real property provided to this Court by the third party, Hainan Zhongbiao Property Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Zhongbiao Company), was real property that Zhongbiao Company had already transferred to the former Jintong City Credit Cooperative (which merged into Hainan Development Bank in December 1997; after Hainan Development Bank was closed in 1998, its claims and debts were taken over by the Haifengxing Liquidation Group). Subsequently, after numerous complaints by the Haifengxing Liquidation Group, this Court discovered and corrected the original enforcement act through Order 9-16. Therefore, Order 9-16 and the enforcement act thereunder merely restored the disputed real property to its property rights status at the beginning of the enforcement case, and there is no causal relationship between this act and the claims determined in the judgment in favor of Guotai Haikou Business Department, nor with its unspecified claims for losses.

2. Order 9-16 and the enforcement act thereunder were not based on the civil judgment (2003) Hai Zhong Fa Min Zai Zi No. 37 of Haikou Intermediate Court; they merely coincided under a unified judicial principle. The term "理当" (should logically) used in the compensation decision of this Court should not be interpreted as "basis."

3. The claims determined in the judgment in favor of Guotai Haikou Business Department had already been transferred to Guotai Investment Company before this Court issued the termination enforcement order (1999) Qiong Gao Fa Zhi Zi No. 9-18 on August 4, 2006, and Guotai Investment Company had already lawfully declared these claims in the bankruptcy liquidation of Haiguozu Company. Therefore, Guotai Haikou Business Department should not apply for state compensation.

The State Compensation Commission of this Court, upon trial, finds:

On September 21, 1998, Hainan High Court, in the case of securities repurchase dispute between the plaintiff Guotai Securities Co., Ltd. Haikou Business Department (predecessor of the compensation claimant Guotai Haikou Business Department, hereinafter collectively referred to as Guotai Haikou Business Department) and the defendant Haiguozu Company, rendered civil judgment (1998) Qiong Jing Chu Zi No. 8. The main text of the judgment is as follows: 1. Haiguozu Company shall pay Guotai Haikou Business Department the principal amount of RMB 36.2 million for the securities repurchase and interest on that amount up to November 30, 1997, of RMB 16,362,296; 2. Haiguozu Company shall pay Guotai Haikou Business Department interest on the principal amount of RMB 36.2 million for the securities repurchase, calculated at an annual interest rate of 18% from December 1, 1997, until the date of full payment; 3. Guotai Haikou Business Department's other claims are dismissed.

In December 1998, Guotai Haikou Business Department applied to Hainan High Court for enforcement of the judgment. After accepting the case, Hainan High Court issued an enforcement notice to Haiguozu Company. Upon investigation, Haiguozu Company had no property available for enforcement. Haiguozu Company provided Hainan High Court with information that it had a claim against a third party, Zhongbiao Company, which had become due. Hainan High Court then served a notice of performance of due debt on Zhongbiao Company. Zhongbiao Company did not raise any objection within the specified 15-day performance period, acknowledged the debt, and expressed its willingness to directly offset part of its debt owed to the judgment debtor Haiguozu Company by transferring some of its real property in Jingrui Building to Guotai Haikou Business Department. On June 13, 2000, Hainan High Court made Order 9-10, sealing part of the real property belonging to Zhongbiao Company located in Jingrui Building, and published a notice on the same day.

On June 29, 2000, Guotai Haikou Business Department, Haiguozu Company, and Zhongbiao Company jointly signed an Enforcement Settlement Agreement. The contents are as follows: 1. Haiguozu Company and Zhongbiao Company shall offset the debt owed to Guotai Haikou Business Department with certain real properties belonging to Zhongbiao Company located at No. 1 Guomao Avenue, Haikou, in Jingrui Building; 2. The offset real properties include: the 7th, 8th, 9th, and 17th floors of Office Building A, totaling 4,440.61 sqm; rooms on the 5th, 6th, 7th, 8th floors and room 901 on the 9th floor of Apartment Building B, totaling 2,759.45 sqm; and the ground floor business hall of Apartment Building B, 882.36 sqm, with a total area of 8,082.42 sqm; 3. The offset price is an average of RMB 5,737 per sqm, with a total offset amount of RMB 46,367,600; 4. Upon confirmation of this agreement by order of Hainan High Court, the ownership of the offset real property shall vest in Guotai Haikou Business Department; Haiguozu Company and Zhongbiao Company shall have an obligation to assist in the property registration procedures.

On June 30, 2000, Hainan High Court made Order 9-11. The order states: "In accordance with the effective civil judgment (1998) Qiong Jing Chu Zi No. 8 of Hainan High People's Court, this Court issued an enforcement notice to the judgment debtor on January 18, 1999, ordering the judgment debtor to perform by January 23, 1999, but the judgment debtor has failed to perform the obligations determined in the effective legal instrument. Upon investigation, the judgment debtor has no property available for enforcement, but has provided this Court with evidence that it holds a due claim against a third party of over RMB 200 million. Accordingly, pursuant to Article 61 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Enforcement Work of People's Courts (Trial), on June 14, 2000, this Court served a notice of performance of due debt (Order (1999) Qiong Gao Fa Zhi Zi No. 13-4) on the third party, ordering the third party to perform the debt of RMB 69 million owed to the judgment debtor in favor of the enforcement applicant within 15 days of receiving the notice. The third party raised no objection within the specified 15-day period, acknowledged owing the judgment debtor over RMB 200 million, and expressed its willingness to directly offset part of its debt by transferring certain real properties located at No. 1 Guomao Avenue, Haikou, Jingrui Building to the enforcement applicant. On June 29, 2000, the enforcement applicant, the judgment debtor, and the third party voluntarily reached a settlement agreement. Based on this agreement, and in accordance with Article 221 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 65 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Enforcement Work of People's Courts (Trial), it is ordered as follows: 1. The due claim of RMB 69 million that the judgment debtor holds against the third party is compulsorily enforced. 2. In accordance with the agreement of the enforcement applicant, judgment debtor, and third party, the following real properties of the third party, Hainan Zhongbiao Property Development Co., Ltd., located at No. 1 Guomao Avenue (intersection of Guomao Avenue and Longkun North Road), Haikou, in Hainan Jingrui Building (formerly Hainan Tangyanjiu Building): Block A (Office Building): 7th, 8th, 9th floors, each with an area of 1,150.09 sqm, and 17th floor, area 990.34 sqm, totaling 4,440.61 sqm; Block B (Apartment Building): ground floor business hall, area 882.36 sqm, 5th floor, area 625.03 sqm, 6th, 7th, 8th floors, each with an area of 647.02 sqm, room 901 on 9th floor, area 151.22 sqm, totaling 3,599.67 sqm. The total area of the above real properties is 8,040.28 sqm (subject to the area approved by the property management authority). At an average price of RMB 5,766.9 per sqm, the total amount is RMB 46,367,600, which is offset to the enforcement applicant, Guotai Junan Securities Co., Ltd. Haikou Binhai Avenue (Tianfu Hotel) Securities Business Department. 3. The sealing of the above real properties and rooms 902, 903, 904 of Block B is lifted." After the order was made, given that some of the real properties were already under enforcement by other courts, when Hainan High Court enforced the order, the actual area offset was 7,049.94 sqm, at an average price of RMB 5,766.90 per sqm, with an offset amount of RMB 40,656,298.

During the process of property transfer registration, third parties, the Haifengxing Liquidation Group and Chuangren Company, raised enforcement objections to Hainan High Court, claiming that the real properties offset under Order 9-11 belonged to them and that the order harmed their lawful rights and interests. The Hainan Provincial People's Procuratorate also issued a procuratorial opinion (2001) Qiong Jian Min Xing Yi Zi No. 1, stating that Zhongbiao Company and Haiguozu Company, in the Enforcement Settlement Agreement with Guotai Haikou Business Department, concealed the truth by using real properties already sold to others for debt offset, constituting malicious collusion between Zhongbiao Company and Haiguozu Company, which seriously damaged the lawful rights and interests of the Haifengxing Liquidation Group, and recommending that Hainan High Court review Order 9-11. Hainan High Court, after review, made Orders 9-12 and 9-13 on September 6, 2000, and May 16, 2001 respectively, dismissing the objections of the Haifengxing Liquidation Group and Chuangren Company. On March 14, 2002, Guotai Haikou Business Department, in accordance with Order 9-11 of Hainan High Court, completed the registration of the property rights of the above offset real properties in its own name and paid relevant taxes and fees of RMB 1,530,647.19.

The Haifengxing Liquidation Group and Chuangren Company, dissatisfied with Orders 9-12 and 9-13 of Hainan High Court, appealed to Hainan High Court. After review, Hainan High Court made Order 9-16 on July 31, 2003. The order states: Chuangren Company, as the developer, sold real properties in Jingrui Building to Zhongbiao Company; Zhongbiao Company then sold part of the Jingrui Building properties to Hainan Development Bank (formerly Jintong City Credit Cooperative); Hainan Development Bank (hereinafter referred to as Haifengxing) had paid 69% of the total purchase price, i.e., RMB 44,830,018.96, to Zhongbiao Company. Applying the principle of fairness under civil law and taking into account the judicial practice of Hainan Province in the trial of pre-sale housing disputes during the real estate boom period, where a contract cannot be performed and the buyer has paid most of the price and the seller is unable to refund, the property should be transferred in proportion to the price paid. Order 9-11 treated the properties purchased by Haifengxing from Zhongbiao Company and for which most of the price had been paid as Zhongbiao Company's properties for offset to Guotai Haikou Business Department, harming the interests of Haifengxing. This was indeed improper. The objection of the Haifengxing Liquidation Group is well-founded; Orders 9-11 and 9-13 should be revoked, and the Jingrui Building properties already enforced under the name of Guotai Haikou Business Department should be recovered. Regarding the objection of Chuangren Company, since Order 9-11 is to be revoked, Order 9-12 should accordingly be revoked as well; Chuangren Company's objection must be resolved through litigation proceedings. As this Court has remanded the case of Haifengxing Liquidation Group v. Zhongbiao Company for confirmation of property rights purchase to Haikou Intermediate Court for retrial, Chuangren Company may participate in that litigation as a third party and seek resolution together. Based on the above, it is ordered as follows: 1. Orders 9-11, 9-12, and 9-13 are revoked; 2. The real properties located at Jingrui Building Block A (Office Building) 7th, 8th, 9th floors, Block B (Apartment Building) ground floor business hall, 5th, 6th, 7th, 8th, and 9th floors (room 901 only), with a total area of 7,049.94 sqm, for which the property title has been registered under the name of Guotai Haikou Business Department, are to be recovered and transferred back to the name of Chuangren Company.

Pursuant to Order 9-16 of Hainan High Court, the disputed real property was recovered to Chuangren Company's name. In June 2005, Guotai Haikou Business Department applied to the Haikou Local Taxation Bureau for a tax refund, and the Haikou Local Taxation Bureau refunded deed tax of RMB 1,219,692.25 to Guotai Haikou Business Department.

On August 4, 2006, Hainan High Court made civil order (1999) Qiong Gao Fa Zhi Zi No. 9-18, ruling that, as Haiguozu Company had been declared bankrupt for debt repayment and the Haiguozu Company Liquidation Group's request to terminate enforcement was well-founded, the enforcement of the civil judgment (1998) Qiong Jing Chu Zi No. 8 of this Court was terminated.

It is also found: On July 9, 2001, the Haifengxing Liquidation Group filed a lawsuit for confirmation of property rights in Haikou Intermediate Court regarding the purchase of properties from Zhongbiao Company by the former Jintong City Credit Cooperative. Haikou Intermediate Court rendered civil judgment (2001) Hai Zhong Fa Min Chu Zi No. 77, holding that the property sale contract was valid and rescinding it, ordering Zhongbiao Company to return the purchase price, interest, and liquidated damages to the Haifengxing Liquidation Group. The Haifengxing Liquidation Group appealed. On July 3, 2002, Hainan High Court rendered civil judgment (2002) Qiong Min Yi Zhong Zi No. 2, dismissing the appeal and affirming the original judgment.

On October 20, 2003, the Hainan High People's Court rendered civil ruling (2003) Qiong Min Zai Zhong Zi No. 29-2, setting aside its civil judgment (2002) Qiong Min Yi Zhong Zi No. 2 and the civil judgment (2001) Hai Zhong Fa Min Chu Zi No. 77 of the Haikou Intermediate People's Court, and remanding the property right confirmation case to the Haikou Intermediate People's Court for retrial. After retrial, the Haikou Intermediate People's Court, in the case concerning the dispute over property right confirmation with the Hainan Development Bank Liquidation Group as plaintiff, Zhongbiao Company as defendant, and Chuangren Company as third party, rendered civil judgment (2003) Hai Zhong Fa Min Zai Zi No. 37 on December 18, 2004. The main text of the judgment is as follows: 1. Confirming that Chuangren Company owns all of the seventh and eighth floors, and 1,085 square meters of the ninth floor of Block A (office building) of Jingrui Building, totaling 3,385 square meters of property; 2. Confirming that the Hainan Development Bank Liquidation Group owns 882.86 square meters of the first-floor shopping mall of Jingrui Building, 65 square meters of the ninth floor, and the tenth, fifteenth, and sixteenth floors of Block A (office building), and the fifth, sixth, seventh, eighth floors and unit 901 of the ninth floor of Block B (apartment building); ordering Chuangren Company to directly deliver the above properties to the Hainan Development Bank Liquidation Group within thirty days from the effective date of this judgment and to assist in handling the property ownership transfer procedures; 3. Dismissing the other claims of the Hainan Development Bank Liquidation Group. This judgment has become legally effective.

It was further found that: On December 12, 2001, Guotai Junan Securities Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Guotai Securities Company) and Shanghai State-owned Assets Management Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Shanghai State-owned Assets Company) entered into a creditor's rights transfer agreement, stipulating that Guotai Securities Company would transfer to Shanghai State-owned Assets Company the creditor's rights it held with a book value of approximately RMB 3.125 billion, including the interest, liquidated damages, and compensation for losses attached to the creditor's rights, at a transfer price of RMB 1.8 billion based on the assessed value. Shanghai State-owned Assets Company would pay RMB 1.4 billion to Guotai Securities Company, with the remaining RMB 400 million recorded as a liability of Shanghai State-owned Assets Company to Guotai Securities Company, to be repaid within five years from the effective date of the agreement. As confirmed by Wu Gang, the agent ad litem of the Guotai Haikou Business Department, the transferred creditor's rights included the creditor's rights of the Guotai Haikou Business Department as determined by civil judgment (1998) Qiong Jing Chu Zi No. 8. On July 27, 2004, Shanghai State-owned Assets Company, Guotai Securities Company, and Guotai Investment Company entered into a tripartite agreement, stipulating that Guotai Securities Company would transfer to Guotai Investment Company the creditor's rights originally transferred to Shanghai State-owned Assets Company.

On November 29, 2005, Hai Guozu Company applied to the Haikou Intermediate People's Court for bankruptcy liquidation. On March 17, 2006, the Haikou Intermediate People's Court ruled to initiate bankruptcy liquidation. During the bankruptcy liquidation process of Hai Guozu Company, Guotai Securities Company, the Tianjin Chifengdao Business Department of Guotai Securities Company, and Guotai Investment Company each submitted claims to the administrator of Hai Guozu Company, with claimed amounts of RMB 9,598,800, RMB 91,120, and RMB 145,091,724 respectively. The claims submitted by Guotai Investment Company included the creditor's rights it acquired from the Guotai Haikou Business Department as determined by civil judgment (1998) Qiong Jing Chu Zi No. 8. The Haikou Intermediate People's Court rendered civil rulings (2005) Hai Zhong Fa Po Zi No. 4-140, 4-156, and 4-332 with respect to the above claims, confirming the creditor's rights of Guotai Securities Company as RMB 8,538,080, the creditor's rights of the Tianjin Chifengdao Business Department of Guotai Securities Company as RMB 91,120, and the creditor's rights of Guotai Investment Company as RMB 142,604,197.72.

According to the distribution plan for the bankruptcy estate of Hai Guozu Company, the amount allocated to 225 ordinary unsecured creditors in the third priority of bankruptcy liquidation was zero, with a distribution ratio of zero. On March 31, 2009, the Haikou Intermediate People's Court rendered civil ruling (2005) Hai Zhong Fa Po Zi No. 4-350, ruling that the bankruptcy liquidation proceedings of Hai Guozu Company be terminated on the ground that the bankruptcy estate had been fully distributed and there were no remaining assets available for distribution.

On December 27, 2010, the Guotai Haikou Business Department filed an application for state compensation with the Hainan High People's Court on the ground of erroneous enforcement by that court. On July 4, 2011, the Hainan High People's Court rendered compensation decision (2011) Qiong Fa Pei Zi No. 1. The decision held that: In accordance with Article 38 of the State Compensation Law, state compensation may be claimed only if the enforcement act was erroneous. In this case, the three requests made by the Guotai Haikou Business Department were in substance all challenges to Ruling No. 9-16 of the Hainan High People's Court, i.e., the assertion that Ruling No. 9-16 was erroneous. In this regard, the Guotai Haikou Business Department could only seek recourse through the appeal procedure according to law. In fact, the Guotai Haikou Business Department had already filed an appeal with the Supreme People's Court on this matter. Its request for compensation on the ground that Ruling No. 9-16 was erroneous had no legal basis. Furthermore, the Guotai Haikou Business Department argued that Ruling No. 9-16 was erroneous because it set aside Rulings No. 9-11, No. 9-12, and No. 9-13 of the Hainan High People's Court, conflicted with the facts found in civil judgment (2001) Hai Zhong Fa Min Chu Zi No. 77 of the Haikou Intermediate People's Court and civil judgment (2002) Qiong Min Yi Zhong Zi No. 2 of the Hainan High People's Court, and that Rulings No. 9-11, No. 9-12, and No. 9-13 were all correct. The facts found by the Hainan High People's Court showed that although civil judgment (2001) Hai Zhong Fa Min Chu Zi No. 77 of the Haikou Intermediate People's Court did not support the Hainan Development Bank's request to confirm its ownership of part of the properties involved in this case, and civil judgment (2002) Qiong Min Yi Zhong Zi No. 2 of the Hainan High People's Court affirmed that judgment, both judgments had been retried in accordance with the law and were set aside by civil judgment (2003) Hai Zhong Fa Min Zai Zi No. 37 of the Haikou Intermediate People's Court, which confirmed that the ownership of the properties involved in this case belonged to Chuangren Company and the Hainan Development Bank respectively, and this judgment had become effective. Pursuant to Article 210 of the Civil Procedure Law, if after execution is completed, the judgment, ruling, or other legal document based on which the execution was carried out is found to be erroneous and is set aside by a people's court, the people's court shall render a ruling ordering the person who obtained the property to return it; if the person refuses to return it, compulsory execution shall be carried out. Accordingly, after civil judgment (2001) Hai Zhong Fa Min Chu Zi No. 77 and civil judgment (2002) Qiong Min Yi Zhong Zi No. 2 were lawfully set aside and civil judgment (2003) Hai Zhong Fa Min Zai Zi No. 37 became effective, the Hainan High People's Court should have lawfully rendered a ruling on restitution to restore the properties involved to their pre-execution status. The assertion of the Guotai Haikou Business Department that the restitution by the Hainan High People's Court was erroneous had no factual or legal basis. Now that Hai Guozu Company had been ruled to be in bankruptcy, the Guotai Haikou Business Department could exercise its rights and assert its interests in accordance with the law. In summary, the reasons given by the Guotai Haikou Business Department for requesting state compensation from the Hainan High People's Court were not valid. Accordingly, it was decided that the compensation application filed by the Guotai Haikou Business Department be rejected and no compensation be granted.

The above facts were not disputed by either the Guotai Haikou Business Department or the Hainan High People's Court, and were supported by the following documents: civil judgment (1998) Qiong Jing Chu Zi No. 8; civil rulings (1999) Qiong Gao Fa Zhi Zi No. 9-10, 9-11, 9-12, 9-13, 9-16, 9-17, 9-18; procuratorial opinion (2001) Qiong Jian Min Xing Yi Zi No. 1; civil judgment (2003) Hai Zhong Fa Min Zai Zi No. 37; civil rulings (2005) Hai Zhong Fa Po Zi No. 4-140, 4-156, 4-332, 4-350; compensation decision (2011) Qiong Fa Pei Zi No. 1; as well as the Execution Settlement Agreement entered into by the Guotai Haikou Business Department, Hai Guozu Company, and Zhongbiao Company; the Creditor's Rights Transfer Agreement entered into by Guotai Securities Company and Shanghai State-owned Assets Company; the Agreement entered into by Guotai Securities Company, Shanghai State-owned Assets Company, and Guotai Investment Company; the Explanation on the Debt Swap of Guotai Junan Securities Co., Ltd. and the Explanation on the Taxation and Tax Refund for the Property Used to Satisfy the Debt at Jingrui Building submitted by the Guotai Haikou Business Department.

The Compensation Commission of this Court is of the opinion that the focus of the dispute in this case lies in the nature of Ruling No. 9-16 of the Hainan High People's Court, the substance of the alleged injury claimed by the Guotai Haikou Business Department, and whether there is a causal relationship between that injury and Ruling No. 9-16 and the acts of the Hainan High People's Court. Based on the above facts, the Compensation Commission of this Court finds as follows:

1. Examination of the nature of Ruling No. 9-16 of the Hainan High People's Court.

During the enforcement of civil judgment (1998) Qiong Jing Chu Zi No. 8, the Hainan High People's Court, acting on information provided by the judgment debtor Hai Guozu Company, and in circumstances where the third party Zhongbiao Company acknowledged the matured debt but concealed the fact that it had entered into a sales contract with an outsider and received most of the purchase price, and where the Guotai Haikou Business Department, Hai Guozu Company, and Zhongbiao Company had entered into an Execution Settlement Agreement, recognized the tripartite settlement agreement by ruling and enforced the disputed properties. Subsequently, the outsiders Hainan Development Bank Liquidation Group and Chuangren Company raised an execution objection. After the Hainan High People's Court dismissed the objection by ruling, they filed a property right confirmation action regarding the disputed properties and repeatedly submitted appeals regarding the execution objection. Upon re-examination, the Hainan High People's Court found that the reasons for the execution objection raised by the Hainan Development Bank Liquidation Group and Chuangren Company were valid, and accordingly rendered Ruling No. 9-16, correcting the original enforcement act and restoring the disputed properties to their state prior to enforcement. The above enforcement acts occurred between 1998 and 2003, and should be governed by the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC (1991) and the relevant provisions of the Supreme People's Court's Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Work of Enforcement by the People's Courts (for Trial Implementation). Pursuant to Article 208 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC (1991) and Articles 70 and 73 of the Supreme People's Court's Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Work of Enforcement by the People's Courts (for Trial Implementation), Ruling No. 9-16 of the Hainan High People's Court was a ruling made in the enforcement procedure, upon finding that the execution objection raised by an outsider was valid, setting aside the original enforcement ruling and restoring the disputed properties, which were not the specific property directed to be delivered by the legal document, to their state prior to enforcement. The term "judgment or ruling that is erroneous" in Article 208 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC (1991) refers to the original effective judgment or ruling that serves as the basis for enforcement, not to rulings made in the enforcement procedure. Ruling No. 9-16 of the Hainan High People's Court did not change the original enforcement basis, did not require trial supervision proceedings, and the ruling and the acts thereunder did not fall within the scope of restitution under Article 214 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC (1991). Although there were certain improprieties in the timing and specific operations of the Hainan High People's Court in issuing Ruling No. 9-16 and in initiating the retrial proceedings for the original property right confirmation action, taking the entire case into consideration, the ruling and the acts thereunder did not violate the provisions of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC (1991) and relevant judicial interpretations, and were corroborated by the content of the effective civil judgment (2003) Hai Zhong Fa Min Zai Zi No. 37 of the Haikou Intermediate People's Court, and the substantive handling was not improper. Therefore, Ruling No. 9-16 and the acts thereunder of the Hainan High People's Court do not constitute the type of illegal infringement as provided for in the State Compensation Law and its judicial interpretations. The reason asserted by the Guotai Haikou Business Department that the ruling should be confirmed as unlawful is not valid.

2. The substance of the alleged injury claimed by the Guotai Haikou Business Department and whether there is a causal relationship between that injury and Ruling No. 9-16 and the acts of the Hainan High People's Court.

Civil judgment (1998) Qiong Jing Chu Zi No. 8 of the Hainan High People's Court imposed on Hai Guozu Company an obligation to pay a sum of money to the Guotai Haikou Business Department, not an obligation to deliver the disputed properties. That is, the creditor's rights lawfully enjoyed by the Guotai Haikou Business Department were the principal and interest of securities repurchase funds, not the disputed properties. The enforcement of the disputed properties was a specific enforcement measure taken by the Hainan High People's Court, upon recognizing the tripartite Execution Settlement Agreement, to realize the lawful creditor's rights of the Guotai Haikou Business Department. The judgment debtor Hai Guozu Company had no ability to satisfy its debts. Because it had a matured creditor's right against the third party Zhongbiao Company, and Zhongbiao Company did not object but acknowledged the performance of that debt, while concealing the fact that it had entered into a sales contract with an outsider and received most of the purchase price, and entered into the tripartite Execution Settlement Agreement with the Guotai Haikou Business Department and Hai Guozu Company, which was materially defective due to infringement of the lawful rights of an outsider, the property rights in the disputed properties obtained by the Guotai Haikou Business Department under Ruling No. 9-11 issued by the Hainan High People's Court based on that agreement are not protected by law. Ruling No. 9-16 of the Hainan High People's Court set aside Ruling No. 9-11 and restored the disputed properties to their state prior to enforcement. This act was also corroborated by the content of the effective civil judgment (2003) Hai Zhong Fa Min Zai Zi No. 37 of the Haikou Intermediate People's Court, and the substantive handling was not improper. Therefore, the reason asserted by the Guotai Haikou Business Department in its application that it had lawfully obtained property rights in the disputed properties and that Ruling No. 9-16 of the Hainan High People's Court infringed its lawful property rights is not valid. The substance of the failure to realize the creditor's rights determined by the judgment in favor of the Guotai Haikou Business Department lies in the fact that the judgment debtor Hai Guozu Company had no ability to satisfy its debts. Although the Guotai Haikou Business Department and its assignees of the creditor's rights submitted claims in the bankruptcy proceedings, they were still unable to obtain satisfaction. The third party Zhongbiao Company was at fault in performing the matured debt, the tripartite Execution Settlement Agreement was materially defective due to infringement of the lawful rights of an outsider, and the original enforcement acts based on that agreement should be corrected according to law. Therefore, there is no legal causal relationship between the failure to realize the creditor's rights determined by the judgment in favor of the Guotai Haikou Business Department and Ruling No. 9-16 and the enforcement acts of the Hainan High People's Court.

In summary, Ruling No. 9-16 and the enforcement acts of the Hainan High People's Court do not constitute the type of illegal infringement as provided for in the State Compensation Law and its judicial interpretations. The matters and reasons asserted by the Guotai Haikou Business Department in its application lack legal basis and should not be supported. Compensation decision (2011) Qiong Fa Pei Zi No. 1 of the Hainan High People's Court has clear findings of fact and correct application of law, and should be affirmed. Pursuant to Article 24, paragraph 3, Article 29, and Article 38 of the State Compensation Law of the PRC, Article 4 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning Judicial Compensation in Civil and Administrative Litigation, Article 2 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the State Compensation Law of the PRC (I), and Articles 19(1) and 20 of the Supreme People's Court's Provisions on the Procedure for the Compensation Commission of the People's Court to Hear State Compensation Cases, the Compensation Commission of this Court decides as follows:

Affirm the compensation decision (2011) Qiong Fa Pei Zi No. 1 of the Hainan High People's Court.

This decision is a legally effective decision.

March 23, 2012
